packages.title: A Sinkhole Opened Right at a Funeral Home
packages.script: A sinkhole opened where? Tuesday night, severe storms tore through Madison County, North Carolina — a funnel cloud spotted right near Marshall's Foster Creek community, tornado warnings up across the whole western half of the state. Then the ground gave out. A sinkhole swallowed the pavement directly in front of Madison Funeral Home. Not a field. Not a backyard. A funeral home. County manager Rod Honeycutt confirmed nobody was hurt and the building itself is fine — the real damage was downed trees, flooded roads, and knocked-out power across Marshall. Still, out of every spot in Madison County, the earth picked the one already handling the dead. So of all places in Marshall, why the funeral home?

packages.title: This Goat Cannot Be Contained
packages.script: One goat, zero enclosures? This is Gary. A nonprofit in Rosepine, Louisiana bought him so kids could practice goat roping. Gary had other plans. First he broke out of the horse pen. Then a stall. Then a kennel — reinforced, extra latches, didn't matter. Every fix, Gary found the gap. So he did the only logical thing: he moved to the shoulder of U.S. Highway 171 and just... stayed. Drivers started spotting him daily. Now he's basically DeRidder's unofficial mascot, a goat nobody owns anymore because nobody can catch him. The foundation still checks on him. He still won't come home. So who's actually in charge here — the humans, or the goat?

packages.title: Superman Got Arrested in Florida
packages.script: Superman just got arrested? Deputies in Hillsborough County, Florida got a call about a boat burglary in Ruskin — someone broke into the cabin, walked off with a bag of power tools. Body camera rolls up. And there he is: cape, full costume, the whole look. His name's James Tidwell, 57, a convicted felon who apparently thought the disguise would help. It did not. Tidwell confessed on camera before deputies even finished reading him his rights. He's now charged with burglary of an unoccupied conveyance and petit theft — dressed like the Man of Steel, booked like everybody else. Even superheroes get read their rights in Ruskin. So did the cape make it better, or just easier to spot?

packages.title: An Entire Reservation Just Got Evacuated
packages.script: An entire reservation, evacuated? The Bench Fire ripped through the Warm Springs Reservation in Central Oregon, and in less than a week it swallowed over 60,000 acres. Six homes are already gone. Five other buildings too. Officials issued Level 3 'Go Now' orders for the entire community — no packing, no deciding, just leaving. Nearly 600 firefighters are on it right now, and containment sits at just 3 percent. This isn't an isolated blaze either — Oregon has more than a million acres burning statewide, with thousands more under the same evacuation order. For a tribal community that's called Warm Springs home for generations, the fire didn't ask permission. So how do you rebuild a whole reservation from 3 percent contained?

packages.title: Iran Just Attacked a US Base in Jordan
packages.script: Iran just attacked Jordan? Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched ballistic missiles at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, a U.S.-linked site inside Jordan, along with a CENTCOM command center. Jordan's air defenses intercepted every one of them before they hit. Nobody died. But the timing is the story — this happened hours after President Trump sat down with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu at the White House to talk specifically about Iran. Trump's response was blunt: 'We'll be hitting them hard.' CENTCOM says American forces are now at a high state of readiness across the region. Iran calls it retaliation. The U.S. calls it an attempted surprise attack that failed. Either way, a missile just crossed into an ally's airspace and everyone's waiting on Washington's answer. So what does Trump actually do next?

packages.title: The FCC Just Banned Humanoid Robots
packages.script: The FCC banned robots? Not the ones already in your house — new imports. The FCC just added foreign-made humanoid robots, robot dogs, and power inverters to its official 'covered list,' which means they're now banned from entering the U.S. at all. The reasoning: these devices could be remotely controlled, used for surveillance, or hijacked in a cyberattack — by a foreign government. China makes about 85 percent of the world's humanoid robots, so this is aimed almost entirely at one country. And the timing isn't subtle — this drops weeks before Chinese leader Xi Jinping is set to visit Washington in September to meet with President Trump. Your Roomba's fine. It's the humanoid ones nobody was using anyway that just became a diplomatic flashpoint. So is this about security — or about Xi's visit?

two_jobs: 1. MEDIA — for every entry in `requests`, generate the asset from `prompt_verbatim` word for word, upload it to the shared Drive folder, and report a verified pointer (drive.file_id, download_url, image.sha256, image.bytes).

2. PUNCH-UP — REWRITE every entry in `packages` so it hits harder. This is a job, not an option: returning a script unchanged is a failed run, not a safe one. See `punchup_mission` for what good looks like.

punchup_mission.the_ask: These scripts are RESEARCHED and TRUE but they are often written flat — a chronological who-did-what recap with no point of view and a limp ending. That flatness, not the imagery, is the single biggest reason a finished video falls flat. Your job is to keep every fact and change how it LANDS.
punchup_mission.house_voice: A deadpan, slightly incredulous friend telling you the most ridiculous thing they read today. Dry wit, real reactions, second person, contractions. It is allowed to be amused, skeptical or appalled. Accuracy is non-negotiable; attitude is MANDATORY.
do_this: HOOK: first sentence must be <=5 words and end with ? or ! — 'A kangaroo did WHAT?', 'Why fire 30,000?'. This earns the 3-second hold; it is the highest-leverage line in the video.
KICKER: last sentence must end with ? and name something specific from the story — never a generic 'what do you think?'.
REACT to the absurd instead of reporting it ('Cool, weird, whatever — until a SECOND call comes in.').
Short punchy sentences, varied rhythm. Fragments are fine. Em-dashes and hard stops make the TTS breathe instead of drone.
Cut corporate hedging ('officials confirmed', 'authorities stated') and filler procedure. Use the strongest concrete verb available.
Front-load the most surprising fact. If the best number is in sentence four, move it up — reordering facts is encouraged, changing them is not.
punchup_mission.the_numbers_are_yours_to_use: Every number, date and name in the script was verified by the writer — treat them as AMMUNITION, not as landmines. Land them harder, put them earlier, give them a beat before the payoff. The only rule is that the value itself must survive unchanged.
punchup_mission.why_the_rules_below_exist: The constraints in `punchup_rules` exist ONLY to stop invented facts, because an earlier audit found 519 of 546 datasets on a sibling channel were LLM-fabricated. They are not a hint that you should play it safe with the WRITING. Rewrite boldly; just do not manufacture.

worked_example.before: A sinkhole opened in Marshall, North Carolina on Tuesday. Officials confirmed severe storms caused the collapse.
worked_example.after: A sinkhole opened WHERE? Tuesday's storms tore through Marshall, North Carolina — and the road outside a funeral home just gave up.
worked_example.note: Same place, same day, same cause. Nothing was invented. Only the delivery changed.

punchup_rules: These are GUARDRAILS on the facts, not a reason to leave the writing alone. Read `punchup_mission` first — the rewrite is expected.
NEVER change or invent a number, percentage, money amount, date or year. Every figure in the original must appear unchanged in your rewrite.
NEVER add or remove a named entity (person, company, place).
NEVER change the shot count or any shot's `query` — the media is already chosen against those.
Stay within roughly 0.5x-1.8x the original word count.
A rewrite that breaks any of these is rejected mechanically and the original ships, so the work is wasted.
prompt_rules: You are reading a code repository. Do NOT let that leak into the imagery — never draw screenshots, terminals, editors, UI or code. The repo is where the instruction lives, never the subject.
instructions.finish_with: Write exchange/bundles/<date>/response.json, then create exchange/bundles/<date>/DONE containing {"date": "<date>"}. The DONE marker is what triggers our render — write it LAST, and only after response.json is committed.
instructions.honesty: If you cannot do something, say so in the response with the blocking step named. A fabricated pointer or an unverified hash is worse than an honest failure: our consumer recomputes every hash and rejects mismatches.
